readme_excerpt:
# Slunder Studio

![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.1.34-A293FF)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-58D6CA)
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11%20or%203.12-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)
![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/source-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-172A3A)

**Your private music workstation, from first line to final master.**

Slunder Studio brings song generation, lyric writing, MIDI composition, vocal tools, stem separation, and mastering into one desktop workspace. The creative engines run on your computer once their models are installed. Projects and exports stay under your control.

[**Download Slunder Studio v0.1.34 for Windows**](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/SlunderStudio/releases/tag/v0.1.34) | [Run from source](#run-from-source) | [Choose your models](#models-and-storage)

![Slunder Studio desktop music workstation](.github/social-preview.png)

## Make a track without leaving the workstation

Start with a lyric or production brief. Build the song in Song Forge, compose or edit MIDI, route audio through vocals and stem tools, then prepare the final mix. Every stage remains available as a focused workspace when you want direct control.

description: Verified, deduplicated backups for your DAW projects — that you own. A Lazy Creatives tool.
readme_excerpt:
Lazy Creatives — Backups

Verified, deduplicated backups for your music projects — that you own.

Website · Product page · Pricing · Sibling tool: Uploader

Point it at your project folders and it finds every session (Ableton & FL Studio), follows each one's samples, copies complete de-duplicated snapshots to your own NAS/drive, then **re-reads and re-hashes every file to prove the backup actually opens**. No cloud, no account — you own the storage. > Cloud DAW-sync tools can't make these claims structurally. This can. Part of [**Lazy Creatives**](https://lazycreatives.github.io) — tools that take the boring, behind-the-scenes work of making music off your plate. *Looks lazy. Works obsessively.* --- ## Why - **Your samples never go missing.** It resolves every referenced sample, and if one isn't where the project points, it relinks the *right* file from your library (verified by recorded size, not just filename — so it never silently backs up a different same-named sample). - **Backups are verified, not just copied.** Each snapshot ships a manifest of every file + content hash; after writing, it re-reads the snapshot to confirm nothing was truncated, and you can deep-**Verify** any snapshot on demand (re-hashes every byte, and checks the project would open standalone). - **Space-efficient.** A content-addressed pool + hardlinks mean each dated snapshot is a full, openable project but only costs the bytes that changed. - **Only snapshots when something changed** — no redundant history. - **Multi-DAW.** Ableto

description: Music royalty statement parser: 7 vendor formats to one tied-out dataset and Excel earnings tape. Rust → WebAssembly, runs in the browser at perpendis.com/royalty — files never leave the machine.
readme_excerpt:
# nash-royalty-engine

A Rust engine that parses music royalty statements (DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby,
Symphonic, ASCAP, MLC, publisher CSVs) into one canonical line-item dataset,
proves the extraction with an exact-decimal **tie-out**, and writes the deliverable
a catalog-diligence buyer actually opens — a multi-sheet Excel **earnings tape**.
The same engine compiles to WebAssembly and runs live in the browser at
[perpendis.com/royalty](https://perpendis.com/royalty/), where statements are
parsed entirely client-side — **files never leave the machine**.

## Why it's interesting

- **Money is `rust_decimal::Decimal`, never `f64`.** Extracted rows must sum to
  the statement's reported totals within $0.01, or the statement is flagged
  BROKEN. A statement that reconciles by floating-point accident is worse than
  one that fails loudly.
- **Rows are never silently dropped or coerced.** An unparseable amount is a
  warning with a row number, never a zero. Unmapped source columns are preserved
  as JSON; every line carries the SHA-256 of its source file and its row number.
- **One engine, two targets.** The exact parser/tie-out/xlsx code that runs in
  the CLI is exported over a hand-rolled wasm ABI (no wasm-bindgen, no JS glue
  framework) and does all its work inside the browser tab.

## Results on real data

From [docs/FINDINGS.md](docs/FINDINGS.md) (Aug 2026, validation corpus of real
statements found in public sources — not redistributed here):

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Real + fixture rows parsed | **553,075** across 12 statements |
| Unparseable-amount warnings on real data | **0** (only the deliberately poisoned fixture warns, exactly on its poisoned cells) |
| Wrong-file rejections | 9/9 correct — registration and metadata tables refused, not hallucinated |
| Cross-parser validation | 200k-row file: generic parser and DMP parser agree to the cent ($10,010,176.22) |
| Full-corpus runtime (release build) | **9.6 seconds** (~150MB input) |

description: Self-hosted digital music storefront for indie musicians and small labels
readme_excerpt:
# Merch Table

Merch Table is a Next.js + Prisma app for running a digital music storefront for independent artists and labels.

## Features

- Interactive release catalog management with flexible payment option support
- Intuitive storefront for browsing releases and artists
- Publishes digital releases with flexible format delivery (`MP3`, `M4A`, `FLAC`)
- Handles Stripe checkout and webhook-driven order fulfillment
- Provides buyer library access and signed download links
- Includes an operational setup wizard for first-run configuration
- Runs a background transcode worker for preview and delivery assets

## Stack

- App: Next.js (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4
- Data: Prisma, PostgreSQL, Redis
- Auth and Validation: Better Auth, Zod
- Storage and Media: AWS SDK v3 (S3-compatible APIs), bundled Garage or external S3 provider, FFmpeg/FFprobe worker pipeline
- Email and Payments: Nodemailer (SMTP), Stripe
- Infra: Docker Compose (web, worker, postgres, redis, garage)

## Project Status

- Active build in phased delivery.
- Current planning artifacts:
  - [V1 Build Plan](docs/merch-table-v1-plan.md)
  - [V1 Build Checklist](docs/merch-table-v1-build-checklist.md)

## Documentation

- [Environment Variables Reference](docs/env.md): canonical env var list, defaults, and behavior notes
- [Setup Guide](docs/setup.md): prerequisites, environment, local stack startup, migrations, tests, troubleshooting
- [Worker and Storage](docs/worker-and-storage.md): transcode worker behavior, Garage notes, networking
- [Backup and Migration](docs/backup-and-migration.md): Postgres backups, Garage asset backups, Garage-to-S3 migration runbook, and routine upgrade/rollback steps (including `git pull` + `docker compose up -d --build`)
- [Setup Wizard](docs/setup-wizard.md): bootstrap flow, wizard steps, security behavior, env flags
- [Stripe Local Webhook Testing](docs/stripe-webhooks-local.md): Stripe CLI forwarding and test events
